description: Hi, I'm Dev, a first year engineering undergrad interested in astronomy. I've dreamed of the stars ever since I was kid and this hackathon gives me a platform to showcase my love for the same. Join my team if you are a dreamer, a writer or anyone with a deep love of the fabulous study of space and the universe and humanity's efforts to conquer it.
summary:
The Forerunners of Humanity is an interactive educational web experience honoring ten ended NASA robotic missions: Pioneer 10, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner, NEAR Shoemaker, Spirit, Opportunity, Dawn, Kepler, InSight, and Ingenuity.
Built as an engaging alternative to doomscrolling, it lets visitors drive a rover companion named Pip across a Mars and deep-space map to unlock five-chapter mission stories, spacecraft melodies, fun facts, and official NASA archive links. Heartfelt space quotes appear briefly before major destinations load.
Explorers can build a Daily Explorer streak with Commander Astro, collect Hall of Fame ranks, solve rapid true-or-myth drops and riddles, step through a 52-year timeline, run hands-on experiments in Dr. Nova’s Science Lab, play rover and mission games, chat live with Pip, and listen to warm human narration over optional cosmic ambience.
details:
What it does and how it works
Silent Machines is a mobile-friendly web app that teaches the story of ten ended NASA robotic explorers. A rover guide named Pip drives across an interactive Mars map. When a student taps a numbered mission node, Pip drives there, unlocks that mission’s stamp, and tells its story. Each mission has chapters covering what the machine was, how it worked, launch and end dates, where it rests today, and a link to the NASA source. Narration and optional ambient music (Starlight, Deep Space Drift, Mars Breeze) play alongside the text. An “Ask Pip” feature lets students ask questions.

Benefits

  • Students learn real mission history in short chapters instead of long articles.
  • Quests, XP, stamps, daily streaks, true-or-false drops, riddles and mini-games give a reason to come back.
  • Narration and music make it more accessible for younger and auditory learners.
  • It is free and runs in a phone browser, with no install.

Intended impact
The goal is to make school-age space enthusiasts care about the hardware NASA left behind. These machines paved the way for current and future Mars exploration, and their stories are often overlooked. We want students to leave curious about robotics, planetary science and space careers.

Tools and technology

  • Built as a web app through Google AI Studio.
  • NASA mission facts and sources, with a NotebookLM notebook for organizing research.
  • Voice narration and generated ambient audio.

Creativity
The project turns “dead” missions into characters with voices. The “silent machines” idea frames them as explorers whose stories still deserve to be told. Pip works as friendly guide, quiz host and gameplay mascot. Mixing storytelling, a Mars map, riddles and rewards makes the history feel like an expedition.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: Facts come from NASA sources, with links shown in the app.
  • Audience: Language is warm and simple for school-age learners.
  • Cost: The build had to be zero-cost and free for users.
  • Accessibility: Music and narration are optional, and volume is adjustable.
  • Scope: We focused on Mars to keep the project polished within the hackathon time.
